_note: Curated radio-astronomy and SETI entries. RA/Dec are J2000 degrees. 'approximate' marks positions known only roughly (historic beams, moving probes).

objects.name: Cassiopeia A
objects.description: Brightest extrasolar radio source in the sky at low frequencies; remnant of a supernova seen around 1680.

objects.name: Cygnus A
objects.description: One of the strongest radio galaxies; twin jets feed lobes ~500,000 light-years apart.

objects.name: Taurus A (Crab Nebula)
objects.description: Supernova remnant of SN 1054 and the classic Taurus A radio source; contains the Crab pulsar.

objects.name: Virgo A (M87)
objects.description: Giant elliptical galaxy with a relativistic jet; its central black hole was imaged by the EHT in 2019.

objects.name: Centaurus A
objects.description: Nearest large radio galaxy, with radio lobes spanning about 8 degrees of sky.

objects.name: Sagittarius A*
objects.description: Compact radio source at the Galactic Centre, the Milky Way's 4-million-solar-mass black hole.

objects.name: Hercules A
objects.description: Powerful radio galaxy with spectacular ringed jets.

objects.name: Fornax A
objects.description: Bright southern radio galaxy (NGC 1316).

objects.name: Orion A
objects.description: Thermal radio emission from the Orion Nebula's HII region.

objects.name: 3C 273
objects.description: First quasar identified (1963); optically the brightest quasar in the sky.

objects.name: 3C 48
objects.description: First radio source shown to have a quasi-stellar optical counterpart.

objects.name: Pictor A
objects.description: Radio galaxy with a hotspot ~800,000 light-years from its nucleus.

objects.name: Hydra A
objects.description: Radio galaxy at the heart of a cooling-flow galaxy cluster.

objects.name: Cygnus X-1
objects.description: First widely accepted black hole: an X-ray binary with radio jets.

objects.name: Crab Pulsar (PSR B0531+21)
objects.description: 33 ms pulsar powering the Crab Nebula; giant radio pulses.

objects.name: Vela Pulsar (PSR B0833-45)
objects.description: Brightest persistent radio pulsar; 89 ms period with famous glitches.

objects.name: PSR B1919+21
objects.description: First pulsar discovered (Jocelyn Bell Burnell, 1967); initially nicknamed LGM-1, 'Little Green Men'.

objects.name: PSR B0329+54
objects.description: Brightest pulsar in the northern sky; a favourite target for amateur radio telescopes.

objects.name: PSR B1937+21
objects.description: First millisecond pulsar discovered (1.56 ms).

objects.name: PSR B1257+12
objects.description: Host of the first confirmed exoplanets (1992), orbiting a pulsar.

objects.name: PSR B1913+16 (Hulse-Taylor)
objects.description: Binary pulsar whose orbital decay confirmed gravitational-wave emission.

objects.name: PSR J0437-4715
objects.description: Nearest and brightest millisecond pulsar; a precision timing reference.

objects.name: Wow! signal
objects.description: 72-second narrowband signal near 1420 MHz detected by Big Ear on 15 Aug 1977. Never observed again. The horn beam leaves two candidate RA positions; the first is shown.

objects.name: BLC1 (Proxima Centauri)
objects.description: 982.002 MHz candidate seen by Breakthrough Listen at Parkes in 2019; later attributed to terrestrial interference.

objects.name: SHGb02+14a
objects.description: SETI@home candidate near 1420 MHz observed three times at Arecibo in 2003; most likely noise.

objects.name: KIC 8462852 (Tabby's Star)
objects.description: Star with irregular dips of up to 22%; SETI searches found no artificial signals and dust is the leading explanation.

objects.name: Ross 128 signal
objects.description: Unusual 2017 Arecibo signal near the red dwarf Ross 128, attributed to geostationary satellites.

objects.name: HD 164595 signal
objects.description: 2015 RATAN-600 11 GHz transient; follow-ups found nothing and it is considered terrestrial interference.

objects.name: FRB 20121102A
objects.description: First fast radio burst found to repeat, localised to a dwarf galaxy ~3 billion light-years away.

objects.name: Lorimer Burst (FRB 010724)
objects.description: The first fast radio burst ever recognised, found in archival 2001 Parkes data.

objects.name: SGR 1935+2154
objects.description: Galactic magnetar that emitted a fast radio burst in April 2020, linking FRBs to magnetars.

objects.name: Arecibo message target (M13)
objects.description: Destination of the 1974 Arecibo message, beamed toward globular cluster M13.

objects.name: Hydrogen line (21 cm)
objects.description: 1420.405751 MHz emission of neutral hydrogen, the 'water hole' frequency favoured by SETI. Strongest toward the galactic plane; shown at the Galactic Centre.

objects.name: Voyager 1
objects.description: Most distant human-made object, in interstellar space since 2012 and still transmitting at 8.4 GHz. Position approximate for the mid-2020s.

objects.name: Voyager 2
objects.description: Entered interstellar space in 2018; reachable only from the southern hemisphere (DSS-43). Position approximate for the mid-2020s.

objects.name: New Horizons
objects.description: Pluto and Arrokoth flyby probe, now in the Kuiper Belt. Position approximate for the mid-2020s.

objects.name: Pioneer 10
objects.description: First probe to cross the asteroid belt; silent since 2003, drifting toward Aldebaran.
